text:
alex: HydraBank POC kickoff - they are regulated, want a Private deployment. Main asks: stable egress IPs, TLS inspection in their on-prem appliance, and preserving client cert info/ALPN. They're debating VPC peering vs PrivateLink. Also asked for a minimal firewall/route checklist we can hand to their netops, and a ballpark Dedicated pricing for ~4 GPU seats for a 30-day POC. @maria @jonah any quick thoughts?

maria: high level tradeoffs: peering = layer3 routes -> preserves source IPs, end-to-end TLS untouched. PrivateLink = endpoint svc (NLB) + NAT - client connections terminate at our endpoint so source IP will be our ENI/NAT. If customer needs client cert passthrough or ALPN intact, peering is safer.

jonah: adding practical checklist for both options: 
- VPC peering:
  - Add route table entry: 10.50.0.0/16 -> peering-connection-id
  - Security group on Redwood side: allow inbound from 10.50.0.0/16 TCP 443 (and 80 if needed)
  - Ensure no overlapping CIDRs
  - NACLs: allow ephemeral ports (1024-65535) for response traffic

- PrivateLink:
  - Customer creates interface endpoint in their subnet(s) -> ENIs in their VPC
  - We expose an NLB in our VPC; traffic flows through NLB, we see endpoint IPs (SNAT)
  - Configure SG to allow inbound from endpoint SGs + allow outbound to customer's CIDRs if using backhaul

jonah: firewall example for their appliance (AWS Security Group style):
```
Type: TLS (TCP 443)
Source: 10.50.0.0/16   # peering
Destination: sg-0abc123redwood
Action: ALLOW
```

jonah: and if they insist on PrivateLink and need predictable egress IPs on our side, we can allocate static EIPs on a NAT fleet in our VPC and route traffic out that way (adds complexity + cost).

sam: security questionnaire bullet points to give them:
- Data handling: transient request logs retained X days (configurable).
- KMS integration: customer-supplied keys supported for Private deployments (list supported KMS vendors).
- Audit logs: API + model inference logs (metadata only) available via syslog/S3 with encryption-at-rest.
- Network: support for VPC peering, PrivateLink, dedicated NAT EIPs, and on-prem proxies.
- Compliance: SOC2, ISO27001, dedicated support for contractual BAA/DPAs (if applicable).

sam: also note TLS inspection: if HydraBank does TLS termination for inspection, mutual-TLS or client cert fields will not be visible to our service. ALPN negotiation can be altered by MITM appliances - so any ALPN-based routing will be fragile under TLS inspection. Recommend a test with their appliance in the middle of a tunnel before committing.

alex: customer also asked about pricing: rough quote for Dedicated POC (4x A100-style GPUs equivalent): they asked monthly, but POC is 30 days. Can we give a POC rate + overage?

jonah: rough numbers (very preliminary, subject to procurement):
- Dedicated reserved for POC (4 GPU-equivalent nodes, spot disabled): ~$18k/month list.
- Short-term POC uplift + support + priority queueing: one-time $2k setup + $3k POC premium.
- If they want static EIPs / NAT fleet for egress: +$1.5k/month (infra & EIP allocation).
- If they go Hosted with PrivateLink instead: per-token + endpoint surcharge; cheaper infra but loses source IP preservation.

maria: operational blockers to flag to netops:
- Peering requires both sides to approve and non-overlapping nets.
- PrivateLink may require VPC endpoint quotas increase (ask them to pre-request).
- If they require TLS inspection we need to run an end-to-end test because behavior differs dramatically.

alex: excellent. action items:
- jonah: can you draft the 1-page checklist (routes/SG/NACLs/EIP options) for their netops by EOD?
- sam: attach the high-level answers for the security questionnaire (data retention/KMS/audit)
- maria: confirm whether our Private deployment supports customer-managed HSM for this account (Y/N) and any lead time.

infra-bot: ticket #POC-9347 created -> "HydraBank Private POC network + security checklist" assigned to jonah, sam, maria. ETA: 48h for first draft. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks - I'll forward to the customer's netops and security teams and request a lab window for TLS inspection testing.

jonah: quick note for lab: bring a sample client cert + ALPN-enabled client (http2 h2/alpn) and the customer's TLS inspection appliance config. We need to verify HTTP/2 upgrade and cert fields survive.

maria: also ask them to provide expected CIDR ranges, endpoint subnet IDs, and whether they prefer single-AZ or multi-AZ endpoints for the POC.

alex: sending now.
